**Review round 1** on `08980dda`, reading `1b54485f..08980dda`: **clean** (a blocked round keeps this draft).

| # | lens | severity | finding | where | fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | correctness | medium | The rebuild only drops git's registration of the slot it reuses, not the registration that holds the branch. When the claim takes the `kept` path (crates/runtime/src/lane/mod.rs:847-848, branch exists and is not merged into the base, i.e. a resumed session with unmerged work), the add vector built at mod.rs:845 is `worktree add -q --lock --reason … <path> <branch>` with no `-f`. Git refuses that by documented default when `<branch>` is checked out by another working tree, and the residue after deleting `~/.yi/lanes` is exactly such a registration: a crashed or live slot left at `.git/worktrees/<n>/HEAD = ref: refs/heads/yi/<session>` (mod.rs:985-1000 detaches only a clean hand-back, a dirty orphan stays on its branch). So a user who deletes `~/.yi/lanes` to reclaim disk and then resumes that session still gets a claim failure, now `fatal: '<branch>' is already checked out at '<…/lanes/<hash>/<n>'`, and every later claim of the session fails the same way until someone hand-runs `git worktree prune` — the stranding #664 reports, one error later. `git worktree add -f` is the documented override for precisely this case (`-f` once for a branch checked out elsewhere, twice for a registered-but-missing path), and it is not passed. | `crates/runtime/src/lane/reap.rs:135` | Clear every stale registration whose gitdir path is gone (a `worktree remove`/`prune` sweep over `worktree list --porcelain` under the pool lock) rather than only the reused slot's, or pass `-f` to the add in `add_fresh` so a branch registered at another dead slot path does not refuse the rebuild. |

**Review round 1** on `ed57ea31`, reading `1b54485f..ed57ea31`: **clean** (a blocked round keeps this draft).

| # | lens | severity | finding | where | fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | correctness | medium | The `2>/dev/null` stripper in `read_only_command` deletes any space-separated word that merely *ends* in `/dev/null`, including a word whose real content is a destructive flag with the redirect glued on (the shell terminates a word at an unquoted `>`). `find . -delete>/dev/null` therefore loses `-delete` before classification, leaving `find .`, which the classifier proves Safe, so `bash.kind_for` reports `Read` and `irreversible` reports false. That is the exact failure the PR exists to fix: the parallel scheduler (`crates/runtime/src/tools.rs:409` runs `Read`-kind calls concurrently with other tools) treats a delete as a harmless read, and the advisor's blast-radius flag stays silent. `git branch -Dx>/dev/null` and `find . -name '*.tmp' -delete>/dev/null` take the same path. The same stripper also silently drops the argument a redirect was attached to (`rg needle src>/dev/null` becomes `rg needle`), so its output no longer describes the command that will run. | `crates/tools/src/builtins.rs:303` | Strip only tokens whose pre-`>` text is empty, ASCII digits, or `&` (i.e. a bare redirection such as `2>/dev/null`, `&>/dev/null`, `>/dev/null`), never a token that carries other text; e.g. let `(head, _) = token.split_once('>')` and require `head.is_empty() \|\| head == "&" \|\| head.chars().all(\|c\| c.is_ascii_digit())` before dropping it. Add the glued spellings (`find . -delete>/dev/null`, `git branch -Dx>/dev/null`) to `crates/tools/tests/bash.rs::a_command_that_writes_behind_a_read_verb_is_not_a_read`. |
| 2 | intent | medium | The why's last point is that a lost sandbox stays invisible in CI, and the new `seatbelt()?` rule (this line) is applied to the containment files the diff touches, but four macOS containment tests still return `Ok(())` when Seatbelt is absent: `crates/runtime/tests/claude_hooks/mod.rs:950` (`a_hook_allow_runs_contained_and_the_sandbox_still_refuses_an_escape`), `crates/runtime/tests/claude_hooks/gates.rs:122` (`contained_bash_cannot_write_the_projects_claude_dir`) and `:175`, and `crates/cli/tests/mcp_cli.rs:477` (`a_cell_cannot_plant_a_session_the_host_runs_on_a_fetch`). All four pass silently on a macOS host with no Seatbelt, so the incident the PR exists for is only partly closed, and the change file's claim that "The macOS containment suites fail when Seatbelt is missing where they used to pass" overstates what landed. | `crates/runtime/tests/kernel_sandbox.rs:15` | Replace the four remaining `if !Sandbox::available() { return Ok(()) }` guards with `seatbelt()?` (the runtime and CLI test binaries can each carry the same helper), or narrow the change file's claim to the files converted. |
| 3 | intent | medium | The why names one skip that hides a lost guard, the macOS Seatbelt check, but the diff also turns unrelated environment skips into hard test failures: git in `crates/cli/tests/cli_surfaces.rs` (three undo tests, this line), a tmp-root target dir in `crates/cli/tests/tui_drive.rs:1311`, system python3 in `crates/kernel/tests/kernel_e2e.rs:671` and `crates/tools/tests/tools.rs:2873` and `:3155`. Nothing in the why asks for this, and it changes the suite's contract: `cargo test` now fails on a contributor's machine without git or python3, or whose `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` sits under a tmp root, where it previously passed, and those failures say nothing about the code. | `crates/cli/tests/cli_surfaces.rs:821` | Revert the git, python3 and tmp-root guards to their skips, or split them into their own change with a why (an issue, not this one) so the Seatbelt fix lands on its own ask. |
| 4 | perf | medium | The Performance claim is wrong about this path. read_only_command now runs the classifier twice per invocation, not once: verdict() parses the command, then command_segments() parses it again from scratch (safety.rs:599 and 827 both call parse()), and the whole command is copied into a new String first. The result is not shared with the gate either: runtime/src/tools.rs calls the label three times per bash call (execution_mode:409 via kind_for, the wall check:632 via kind_for, the broker:672 via irreversible), so a single bash call pays roughly six parses plus three full-string copies where it used to pay a whitespace split. Bash is the agent's most frequent tool, so every turn pays this on every call. | `crates/tools/src/builtins.rs:309` | Parse once: call command_segments() a single time and run the Verdict logic over those segments (or have a verdict variant return the segments it parsed), so the label costs one parse; and reuse the vector instead of copying the command through quiet.join. |
| 5 | perf | medium | is_catastrophic folds and normalizes the path at line 234 and then hands the same path to write_is_catastrophic, which folds and normalizes it again (line 244): every call allocates the normalized PathBuf and the lowercased String twice. command_targets_catastrophic runs is_catastrophic once per path token of a destructive command (catastrophic.rs:791-805), so an `rm` with a long argument list pays the duplicate path clone, lowercase and prefix loops for each argument, and every Remove through ReadGate::remove_after pays it too. | `crates/permission/src/catastrophic.rs:234` | Take the folded path once and pass it down: split write_is_catastrophic into a folded-path body that is_catastrophic can call after its own normalize, so the path is normalized and lowered once per call. |
| 6 | reuse | medium | The diff adds the shared `seatbelt()` guard twice (crates/runtime/tests/kernel_sandbox.rs:16, `pub(crate) fn seatbelt() -> TestResult`, and the byte-identical crates/tools/tests/sandbox.rs:16) and then re-spells a third copy inline in the same runtime test binary that already holds the pub(crate) one, instead of importing it as kept_rules.rs:148 and sandbox_seam.rs:245 do; the change file's claim that "60 skip guards became one `seatbelt()?` check per file" is not what lands, and the green-on-missing-Seatbelt gap this PR closes now has three bodies to keep in step. | `crates/runtime/tests/permission_auto.rs:69` | Import `use crate::kernel_sandbox::seatbelt;` and write `seatbelt()?;` at the top of auto_runs_a_contained_python_cell, deleting the inline check; for the tools crate, move the helper into a shared support module (the `#[path = "../../types/tests/support/scratch.rs"] mod scratch;` pattern in crates/tools/tests/integration.rs:7) rather than defining a second copy. |
| 7 | tests | medium | The new read label is the classifier's verdict, and the classifier never proves several commands the deleted READ_ONLY_VERBS list did read-only: `printenv` and `ag` are absent from `SAFE` (safety.rs:23-66) so they fall to `Class::Unknown` -> `Verdict::Contain`, and `env` is in `LAUNDERING` (safety.rs:99-101) -> `Class::Destructive`, so `env \| grep PATH` -> `Verdict::Ask`. Because `BashTool::kind_for` returns Read only when this line holds, and `reads_only` in `PermissionBroker::decide_call` is `matches!(kind, ToolKind::Read \| ToolKind::Ledger)` (crates/runtime/src/permission.rs:553), a user who ran these unasked now gets a prompt (`env \| grep PATH` destroys its way to Ask on every platform; `printenv`/`ag` become Contain, which the broker downgrades to Ask off macOS), the advisor flags them irreversible, and the parallel scheduler stops overlapping them. Nothing in the suite would fail if this broke back: `crates/tools/tests/bash.rs:33` pins only the two `rg` searches as reads, and the one assertion that used to pin an env-prefixed read (`RUST_LOG=debug rg needle src`, the line this diff replaces at tools.rs:1776) was deleted while the only replacement (`LD_PRELOAD=x.so rg needle src`) pins the opposite direction. | `crates/tools/src/builtins.rs:308` | Add `printenv` and `ag` to `SAFE`, and decide explicitly whether a bare/piped `env` is destructive, then pin the read side in `crates/tools/tests/bash.rs` (e.g. `printenv PATH`, `env \| grep PATH`) so the demotion cannot happen silently. |
